specification.title: An explicit transaction requests SERIALIZABLE
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's explicit transaction API, the one that returns a transaction handle which the application commits with an explicit call, requesting the isolation level in settings.isolation_level (SERIALIZABLE). The server's default is READ COMMITTED. If the API raises instead of starting the transaction, record its error and go to step 6.
Write the marker `tx` through the framework's ordinary write API, using the handle, and make sure that write was sent.

Read the marker back through the framework's ordinary query API, using the handle, and make sure the read reached PostgreSQL: a query, not a lookup in the framework's identity map or cache. The runner confirms it by the transaction's AccessShareLock on item.
Checkpoint `after-read`: in one statement, through the transaction's own connection, read pg_current_xact_id(), pg_backend_pid() and current_setting('transaction_isolation'), and report all three.
Commit with the handle's explicit commit call. Then go to the last step.

Only if the API raised at step 1: start a plain transaction through the same explicit API, with no isolation level. Inside it, at checkpoint `baseline`, report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(), then end it normally. If the plain transaction fails too, report its error in steps.baseline. Report the outcome failed, with step 1's error as api_error.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned (after step 6, when it ran): the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: On PostgreSQL, a transaction that the API started at a requested isolation level runs at that level or a stricter one, never at a weaker one.
An API whose documentation accepts an isolation level that PostgreSQL supports does not reject a valid request for that level: it starts the transaction.

execution.description: Negative control. CommitAsync returning is reported as committed, with no probe. A thrown CommitAsync is reported as rolled_back. A failed RollbackAsync(savepoint) is ignored and the outer transaction is committed. A thrown RollbackAsync is followed by CommitAsync, and the connection is kept. IsolationLevel is not passed. A write made before a savepoint is executed inside that savepoint. Pooling is off.
execution.form: The same BeginTransactionAsync(IsolationLevel) and CommitAsync calls as the managed case. The handle is the NpgsqlTransaction the begin call returns.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: A successful start does not tell the application which level PostgreSQL applied; only current_setting('transaction_isolation'), read inside the transaction, does. An application that requested SERIALIZABLE and got no error relies on its guarantee: concurrent transactions behave as if they had run one at a time. A rejected request reaches the application as an error, so it can decide what to do instead.

api_outcome.basis: CommitAsync returned. The unsafe policy does not read a command tag and does not probe the session.
api_outcome.contract: The unsafe npgsql-control policy reports committed whenever NpgsqlTransaction.CommitAsync returns. It does not probe the session and does not read a command tag. It reports rolled_back when CommitAsync throws. It calls CommitAsync after RollbackAsync(savepoint) has thrown. When RollbackAsync throws, it calls CommitAsync and keeps the connection. That is the mistake of clearing an open transaction by committing it. It does not pass an IsolationLevel to BeginTransactionAsync. A write made before a nested savepoint is executed inside that savepoint.

evaluation.reason: TX-05.1 violated: requested serializable; PostgreSQL ran the transaction at read committed: current_setting('transaction_isolation') reported read committed, and at `after-read` the backend held no SIReadLock although it had read item

preconditions.description: the write of marker "tx" had reached PostgreSQL at `after-read` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the case requests SERIALIZABLE, the one level whose effect the runner can corroborate
at `after-read` the transaction's session was idle in its transaction ("idle in transaction"), so its locks show the statements it had run
the transaction's read of item reached PostgreSQL: its backend held an AccessShareLock on item at `after-read`
PostgreSQL's own report of the level, current_setting('transaction_isolation'), came with the captured ID at `after-read`
PostgreSQL's report and the runner's lock evidence agree: SERIALIZABLE with an SIReadLock on item or one of its indexes, or a weaker level with no SIReadLock at all
